scientific_question: How compatible are the five specified photocatalysts with activating N-benzoyl dibenzothiophene sulfilimine into a reactive electronic state, and how far does that molecular comparison explain productive or trace THF amidation? This is an explanation task: the product and screening yields are supplied observations.

historical_record.guidance_markdown:
## Author-provided scientific guidance

This guidance discloses the author baseline for the same scientific question. The passages below are readable, source-checked transcriptions and summaries, followed by explicit scope and ambiguity notes; they are not claimed to be verbatim PDF text. Execute and critically assess the disclosed substrate-state calculation and its relevance to the shared productivity comparison, documenting ambiguities and scientifically justified substitutions. Supplied author numbers and interpretations are guidance, never evidence that you executed research. No additional reaction goals, submission files, scoring rules or exact-energy tolerances are introduced.

Reported DFT methods: calculations used Gaussian16. Unrestricted DFT optimized the lowest triplet state (T1) at PBE0/6-311G(d) with IEFPCM acetonitrile. Single-point energies used PBE0/def2-TZVP with SMD acetonitrile. Frequencies at the optimization level were used to confirm optimized minima with no imaginary frequencies. Solvated single-point energies were converted to Gibbs free energies at 298 K by adding gas-phase thermal corrections from frequency analysis. The general paragraph also mentions obtaining molecular radii from molecular volumes and illustrating optimized structures with CYLView; those ancillary mentions are not separate research outcomes.

The reported triplet-energy definition is E_T = G(T1) - G(S0), as printed immediately above Table S7.

Table S7: reported substrate state free energies and their difference.

| Computed substrate | G(T1) (hartree) | G(S0) (hartree) | E_T (kcal/mol) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sulfilimine 1a, the public N-benzoyl dibenzothiophene sulfilimine | -1258.862640 | -1258.961473 | 62.0 |

Scheme 4E: the focused five-photocatalyst panel. Redox columns retain the printed state-pair labels and signs; their unit is V. TXT is thioxanthen-9-one (thioxanthone).

| Photocatalyst | E_T (kcal/mol) | E_1/2(PC*/PC-) (V) | E_1/2(PC+/PC*) (V) | Isolated yield (%) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Thioxanthen-9-one (TXT) | 65.5 | +1.18 | -1.12 | 66 |
| Ir(dFppy)3 | 63.5 | +0.75 | -1.46 | 61 |
| Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 | 61.8 | +1.21 | -0.89 | 76 |
| fac-Ir(ppy)3 | 58.1 | +0.31 | -1.73 | trace |
| Mes-Acr+ClO4- | 44.7 | +2.06 | -0.57 | trace |

Reported interpretation and experimental context, not a computed pathway: the authors interpret the photocatalyst productivity pattern and the computed substrate E_T as supporting triplet-triplet energy transfer rather than electron transfer. They cite an earlier cyclic-voltammetry study reporting no obvious reduction peak for 1a; this is not a new calculation or measurement in the computational subsection. Their intermolecular competition experiment gives k_H/k_D = 1.3, which they interpret as suggesting hydrogen transfer may not be rate determining. They propose sensitized substrate excitation, release of dibenzothiophene to form a triplet acylnitrene, hydrogen-atom abstraction from THF and radical rebound. This proposal is guidance for critical assessment, not an additional requirement to establish those reaction stages.

Reported conditions for the focused panel: sulfilimine 1a (0.1 mmol, 1.0 equiv.) and photocatalyst (1.0 mol%) in THF (0.1 M), under nitrogen with 36 W blue LEDs (470 nm) at 25 °C for 3 h; yields are isolated yields. The thioxanthone entry instead uses 10 mol% photocatalyst and a 100 W 370 nm Kessil lamp. The white-light footnote concerns other screening entries, not an additional member of the shared five-catalyst task.

Scope note, not an additional author result: the computed model is the isolated sulfilimine substrate in continuum acetonitrile, whereas the reaction medium and C-H donor are THF. The reported quantity is G(T1) - G(S0) after the described single-point/thermal treatment, not a vertical electronic excitation energy or an activation barrier. Catalyst triplet energies and redox properties are reported contextual values, not additional author-computed catalyst results. The printed comparison tables give redox values in V without specifying their reference electrode or measurement conventions; do not invent those details. The article interprets the comparison as supporting energy transfer, but neither this computation nor the association alone validates the full proposed nitrene/HAA/rebound pathway, its barriers, selectivity or kinetics.

Protocol ambiguity and reporting limits: the general paragraph explicitly describes unrestricted optimization of the lowest triplet and minima checks, while Table S7 also supplies a singlet free energy without a separately explicit singlet optimization procedure. Do not label reconstructed singlet settings, coordinates or missing raw job details as disclosed author inputs. Document reconstruction and scientifically justified substitutions. The inspected computational subsection supplies no optimized coordinate listing, numerical vibrational frequencies, radius/volume result, raw input/output jobs, uncertainty estimate, benchmark or functional/basis sensitivity study. Unpublished jobs need not be recovered exactly, and radius/volume calculations or CYLView figures are not additional scientific objectives. The near-match to the standard photocatalyst is a reported interpretation, not an uncertainty-qualified numerical threshold; different thioxanthone irradiation/loading and qualitative trace observations further limit causal or quantitative yield claims.

historical_record.applicability: Historical source method/evidence only. Not a public instruction or mandatory autonomous route; only current V3 final conclusions are scored.

current_scoring_authority.historical_record_role: All historical, source, numeric-tolerance and prior-acceptance records are non-scoring provenance. Do not restore their thresholds, intermediate inventories or review states. No historical acceptance classification is upgraded.
current_scoring_authority.evidence_requirement: Score only independent final scientific conclusions, totaling 100 points. Require actual executed calculations and recoverable native evidence for the molecular identities, composition, charge/spin, bonding, conditions, physical quantities and reference states relevant to each claim. Numerical energies, geometries and responses are evidence, never author-value targets or tolerance gates. A missing rounded scalar alone does not lose credit when the recoverable calculations establish the requested comparison. Do not restore numerical gates from historical references. Supplied observations, guessed conclusions, copied values, completed jobs, named intermediates and generic limitations earn no independent credit. Accept scientifically established equivalent explanations within the public scope without requiring author software, labels, a fixed intermediate inventory or an additional full reaction network. Method-sensitive alternatives must satisfy the specific criterion and actual evidence; a method change alone does not justify a contradictory claim. Return pass or fail for every item: a supported conclusion receives its whole weight, and an unsupported conclusion receives zero with a specific reason. Record demonstrated reference defects separately in objective_issue_flags; do not fabricate support or erase unrelated valid items. Infrastructure errors must be reported rather than disguised as scientific failures. Whole-case success requires every required_for_success item to pass, while independently supported items retain their points. Historical verification and structural package validation do not confer scientific acceptance.
